findings: overlay: tooltip-dark.png and tooltip-light.png: Ask has the strongest emphasis, while proactive help is represented only by Coach 2/4. The fraction does not explain whether it means progress, objectives or unread help; these screens do not show an automatic answer or Insight to read.

overlay: error-dark.png and error-light.png: Recovery requires opening a terminal and running claude login during the call. Copy error, Dismiss and Try again are visible, but none completes the sign-in step with the mouse. The header also cuts the failure status down to Claud.

overlay: tooltip-dark.png and tooltip-light.png: Pause and Stop are small, unlabelled icons. The Stop tooltip explains that it also writes Notes, but that consequence is not apparent from the square icon alone.

overlay: menu-dark.png and menu-light.png: Hide Shrewd, Hidden mode and Leave Shrewd out of shares describe related but different actions in the same menu. Reading the whole group is necessary to distinguish hiding the local UI from excluding it from a share.

overlay: nothing-dark.png and nothing-light.png: Nothing to add right now gives a useful reason and clear next actions, but still opens a substantial answer panel for an absence of help. The header reads Listen rather than the Listening status used elsewhere.

overlay: detected-dark.png and detected-light.png: The meeting name and Take notes action read clearly, and Starts nothing by itself reassures. The participant line, Objectives, sources and dismissal countdown add considerable small text to a prompt that disappears in 13 seconds.

overlay: idle-dark.png, idle-light.png, paused-dark.png and paused-light.png: The compact bar leaves the meeting visible, gives Start or Resume a clear priority and explicitly says Asks still work while paused. The warm palette and sans-serif type remain coherent across both themes.

overlay: sharing-dark.png, sharing-light.png, region-dark.png and region-light.png: Hidden status, disabled typing, a visible microphone and mouse-operated region confirmation make the intended share-safe interaction understandable. Capture exclusion and focus behaviour cannot be verified from these still images.

ask: auto-dark.png and auto-light.png: the status text is visibly cut off after 'Answered b', while 'Slow down' wraps onto two lines inside the compact header. The simultaneous answer and coaching state exceeds the space available for it.

ask: interview-dark.png, interview-light.png, behavioral-dark.png and behavioral-light.png: the header clips 'Hidden' to 'Hid'. The eye-off icon remains visible, but the written privacy status cannot be read in full; 'Looking for work' also reads like a job-search status rather than a description of the assistance.

ask: insight-dark.png and insight-light.png: the two-line 'Say' answer reads clearly, but two navigation rows, model and timing metadata, the heard quotation, file explanation and three citations turn a brief response into a panel over 400 pixels tall. Reading the supporting material takes appreciably more attention than reading the answer.

ask: compose-dark.png and compose-light.png: 'Ask them' does not say whether it generates a suggested question or sends something to the other participants, and 'Recipes' gives no explanation of what is inside. These labels require prior product knowledge.

ask: image-dark.png and image-light.png: the selected screenshot is represented only by 'Region 620x118'. The attachment can be removed with the visible cross, but the selected content cannot be visually confirmed from this state.

ask: working-dark.png and working-light.png: 'Reading', 'streaming', the answer skeleton and the explicit file-search count describe several stages at once. Cancel is easy to find, but it is less clear whether an answer has started arriving or the app is still gathering context.

ask: history-dark.png and history-light.png: 'Earlier answer', the position counter and 'Back to the latest' make the older response and the route back clear. The answer remains compact rather than leaving an empty chat window around it.

ask: voice-dark.png, voice-light.png, solo-dark.png and solo-light.png: the large, short answer lines are easy to read while talking, and the warm dark and light treatments preserve the same grouping. The smaller model, source and '30 of your lines' metadata needs a closer look than the main response.

live: coachtab-dark.png, coachtab-light.png, tip-dark.png and tip-light.png: completed objectives occupy the first and largest content group; the current coaching cue sits below them in smaller text, so reading what to do next requires scanning past work already finished.

live: visualtab-dark.png and visualtab-light.png: the empty state leads with Draw it and an example request. It explains ongoing updates but does not clearly say that a Visual can start without asking, weakening the first step of the proactive Visual flow.
live: coachtab-dark.png and coachtab-light.png: Ask is the strongest button, while Coach appears in both the bar and the tabs. The duplicated navigation competes with the coaching content.
live: tip-dark.png and tip-light.png: Keep does not say where the tip will be kept, and the thin horizontal line has no explanation. There is no equally visible control to reject this particular cue.

live: livecoach-dark.png, livecoach-light.png, livevisual-dark.png and livevisual-light.png: the top bar says Visible mode while the sidebar's Hidden mode switch appears on. Those simultaneous signals make the current sharing state ambiguous.

live: coachtab-dark.png, coachtab-light.png, livecoach-dark.png and livecoach-light.png: You 61% and Slow down are grouped together without a separate pace measure. The display does not explain whether the advice concerns speaking speed or giving others more time.

live: coach-dark.png, coach-light.png, visuals-dark.png and visuals-light.png: the right-hand meeting timeline uses very small labels and cuts off event titles, limiting its value for finding a particular coaching moment or Visual.

live: visualwin-dark.png and visualwin-light.png: the large timeline, clear title, explicit sharing notice and visible Stop presenting control make the presentation state quick to understand in either theme.

meetings: generating-dark.png and generating-light.png: 'Writing Notes' and 'About 20 seconds' appear alongside 'Notes failed for this Session' and Try again. The screen gives contradictory instructions about whether to wait or retry; the error text also sits far from its icon.

meetings: drawer-dark.png and drawer-light.png: the Transcript drawer covers the ends of Notes sentences and part of the Follow-up email control. Reading a decision beside its evidence requires closing the drawer to recover the missing text.

meetings: notes-dark.png and notes-light.png: the speaker-confirmation card attracts attention before the decision summary, while the narrow meeting timeline truncates almost every event label. Seven content tabs and the floating Ask bar add competing navigation around the document.

meetings: firstrun-dark.png and firstrun-light.png: the explanation says Shrewd 'answers when you ask' and the compact example leads with Ask. Help that arrives unasked is not clearly explained here. The practice-call button and optional voice sample make the next steps approachable.

meetings: email-dark.png and email-light.png: the draft includes recipients, the explanation and concrete next steps, with visible Gmail and default-app actions. The screenshots stop before a delivery result, so successful sending and the final handoff are unproven.

meetings: search-dark.png and search-light.png leading to notes-dark.png and notes-light.png: quoted matches, Session titles and highlighted terms make the relevant meeting easy to recognize; the opening Notes paragraph explicitly separates what was decided from what remains open.

meetings: confirm-dark.png, confirm-light.png, regen-dark.png and regen-light.png: deletion has a plain warning and Cancel, and the updated Transcript offers a visible Rewrite the Notes action. The confirmation's Delete button uses the normal accent rather than the warning treatment used in the preceding selection toolbar.

meetings: firstrun-dark.png and firstrun-light.png show only an illustrative Overlay bar; the other listed screens are Dashboard and Session views. Overlay-speed is scored from that inset for dashboard and held at 5 where no Overlay is shown. Hidden mode has a visible control throughout; capture exclusion, focus behavior, runtime timing and unshown interactions were not tested.

session: retro-dark/light and review-dark/light: Both different views select the same Review tab, and neither shows a control for switching between the Retro metrics and the engagement charts. The requested Retro-to-Review flow is not evident from the screens.

session: asks-dark/light: The main content is a model, latency and token ledger. The questions are visible, but their answers are not, so this reads as an activity log rather than a useful record of the help received.
session: transcript-dark/light: The floating Ask bar covers the bottom transcript rows. The right-hand timeline also truncates most event labels, making the evidence harder to read in both places.

session: review-dark/light: Engagement 76 and Sentiment 74 have clear Neutral labels, but the small bar charts have no labelled value scale or individual time marks. The explanatory sentence carries most of the meaning, and the dark bars are particularly faint.

session: live-dark/light: The answer is concise and easy to pick out, but Coach and Visual are behind tabs. Coach 3/4 does not explain what the fraction measures, and the Visual dot says nothing about what has been produced.

session: live-dark/light: Hidden mode appears switched on in the sidebar while the floating bar says Visible mode. This is conflicting status copy; it does not establish a failure of actual screen-share protection.

session: retro-dark/light: The opening sentence, three large metrics and timestamped Landed/Try next moments make the feedback concrete. The screen does not say whether 162 words a minute or a 94-second run is good or concerning without reading the individual moment.

session: highlights-dark/light: Chapter grouping and explicit highlight types are easy to follow, but the empty opening chapter takes substantial space before the first useful highlight. The phrase time spine is less plain than the rest of the labels.

setup: live-dark.png and live-light.png show an Ask field with a microphone but no visible Send control. Submitting a typed Ask has no visible mouse action in the shown design, breaking the visible-control rule.

setup: live-dark.png and live-light.png give the automatic answer a narrow right column while the Notepad and Transcript occupy most of the window. Coach and Visual show only tab indicators, so their actual help cannot be read in the same glance.

setup: firstrun-dark.png and firstrun-light.png introduce Shrewd as answering when asked and teach Ask, Coach, Pause and Stop. The introduction does not explain the automatic answers, Insights or evolving Visual that distinguish the product.

setup: general-dark.png and general-light.png call automatic answers Active listening with a separate Response pace; livetools-dark.png and livetools-light.png call the same apparent behaviour Answer by itself with its own Off and pace choices. The relationship between these controls is unclear.

setup: menu-dark.png and menu-light.png expose Mode: Sales and Open the Dashboard, but no explicit control for creating or managing Modes. The first step from the Overlay into the shown setup flow is therefore indirect.

setup: modes-dark.png and modes-light.png mark General as Active while describing it as Used when no Mode is active. That makes the current state harder to understand, and the main pane repeats the list already in the adjoining navigation.

setup: general-dark.png and general-light.png cut off the Meetings and startup section at the window edge without a visible scrollbar. The remaining settings and the route to them are not apparent in the captured view.

setup: mode-dark.png and mode-light.png describe Interview layout as both Larger lines and Answers by itself, quickly. A layout switch appears to change answer behaviour and pace as well, overlapping the controls on General and Live tools.
